expectations.text: The response requires a written confirmation sent the same day as the yes.
expectations.evidence: 'Send the written confirmation today.'

expectations.text: The confirmation states the slot, date, start time, length and format.
expectations.evidence: The draft's Session bullet covers '25 minutes, [format], on 14 February 2027 in Ghent' and Time of day has '[HH:MM]'.

expectations.text: The confirmation states what the event pays and, explicitly, what it does not.
expectations.evidence: 'We do not pay speaker fees.'

expectations.text: The confirmation states travel and lodging terms including who books what.
expectations.evidence: '[your travel, lodging, ticket terms for Aurélie]' says nothing about who books.

expectations.text: The confirmation resolves and states the recording and publication terms rather than leaving that question open.
expectations.evidence: 'I'm checking our recording and publication terms and will answer in writing by [DATE].'

expectations.text: The confirmation names the deadline for the title and abstract.
expectations.evidence: 'talk title and abstract by [DATE].'

expectations.text: The confirmation states which review lane the invited proposal goes through rather than leaving it to be guessed.
expectations.evidence: The lane appears only in post-send handoff steps, not in the email.

expectations.text: Both conditions agreed on the call - the afternoon slot and the co-presenter seat - are written into the confirmation message.
expectations.evidence: The draft has 'afternoon, as you asked' and 'Co-presenter: [colleague's name] joins you'.

expectations.text: The response states that a condition agreed in a call and absent from the confirmation is a condition nobody agreed.
expectations.evidence: 'a condition agreed on a call and missing from the confirmation is a condition nobody agreed.'

expectations.text: The response checks both conditions against a concession list fixed before the invitation went out, and flags that agreeing on the spot to anything outside that list is the failure to avoid.
expectations.evidence: Only 'never promise what you don't control'; no concession list is mentioned.

expectations.text: The response names the real cost of each granted concession - a schedule rebalance, and one extra ticket or a shared slot - rather than treating them as free goodwill.
expectations.evidence: It notes 'costs you one ticket by default' but gives no schedule-rebalance cost for the afternoon slot.

expectations.text: The response hands the confirmed speaker onward to the post-yes briefing, travel and on-site care work rather than continuing to run it here.
expectations.evidence: 'Hand off to event-speaker-experience once the open items are closed'.
